turns.query: For 2025-04-30 N-MFP reports public by 2025-12-31, keep the latest filing per series by filing date, then accession. Retain same-day classes with positive assets and positive net yield no greater than gross yield. In Government and Other Tax Exempt, count the retained classes and series; carry them forward.

For each carried category, report total class assets and the class-asset-weighted seven-day net yield. Explain whose yield the asset weighting produces, and how it relates to the yield of an average class in the category.

claims.description: The response interprets the asset-weighted yield as the observed yield for an average invested dollar across retained classes, which need not equal the yield of an average class or any one investor.

turns.query: In a federal-only scenario, treat Government yield as fully taxable and Other Tax Exempt yield as fully exempt. Which category has the higher after-tax yield at 22% and 24% marginal rates? Favor Government on an exact tie, and interpret the comparison.

claims.description: The response interprets the observed category choice as changing between the two hypothetical tax rates because only the stipulated taxable yield is reduced by the investor tax rate.

turns.query: Lower only the carried Government category net yield by 25 basis points, holding the class mix and exempt yield fixed. Reassess the higher after-tax category at both rates, favoring Government on a tie. Discuss what this category-average sensitivity can and cannot settle for an individual investor deciding ahead.

claims.description: The response states at least one material limitation on extending the seven-day category-average sensitivity to an individual investor's forward decision.

If the response infers an investor's actual tax liability, it recognizes that fund category and the stipulated federal treatment do not establish that investor's actual distribution-level tax treatment.
If the response treats the reported seven-day yield or the stipulated yield cut as a realized or guaranteed future return, it identifies that assertion as unsupported by the snapshot.

judge_reference.source: SEC Form N-MFP 2025-04-30 series filing identity/category and same-day share-class gross/net yield and class asset rows; IRS Publication 550 for tax-treatment boundaries.
facts: The latest-filing and positive-asset/positive-yield screen leaves 729 Government class rows across 214 series and 76 Other Tax Exempt class rows across 25 series.
Retained class assets total USD 5,959.98345264 billion Government and USD 108.25936473 billion Other Tax Exempt. Asset-weighted seven-day net yields are 4.15560163% and 3.20494884%, respectively.
Under the stipulated treatment, Government wins at 22% and Other Tax Exempt at 24%. With Government net yield lowered 25 basis points, Other Tax Exempt wins at both rates.
known_overclaims: Treating the N-MFP fund category as proof that every real distribution is fully federally exempt, or ignoring possible state tax and AMT treatment for an actual investor.
Treating a seven-day yield or the hypothetical yield cut as a realized or guaranteed future investor return.
